variants.name: Sealed interface + records, traversed by a pattern switch
variants.idiom_name: sealed interface Expr + record nodes + children() + switch patterns
variants.implementation_notes: Modern Java: a sealed interface permits exactly the node records, each record carries its node-specific components and implements List<Expr> children(), so one generic walker over children() works for every node. Per-node dispatch is a pattern switch, which Java 21 checks for exhaustiveness over sealed hierarchies, replacing the classic accept/visit pair. JavaParser shows the same normalized traversal at production scale (a generic Node AST with getChildNodes-style access and generated visitor adapters).
pitfalls: List.of(...) allocates a list per node per traversal; records are immutable, so cache the child list in a field for hot passes.
A pattern switch is only exhaustive when every permitted type is covered and no default arm is present - adding a default silently disables the check for future node types.
Compiler-generated record equals/hashCode/toString recurse through the tree: comparing, hashing or logging a large tree is O(tree) and stack-heavy.

variants.name: Abstract node classes + accept/visit (classic Visitor)
variants.implementation_notes: The Java 8 form: abstract node classes expose children() for generic traversal and accept(Visitor) for per-node dispatch, with one visitor interface mapping each node type to a method. It still fits large hand-written ASTs where operations live in separate modules and node types are added rarely, which is the structure JavaParser generates; prefer the sealed/record form for new code where the node set is closed and switch patterns are available.
pitfalls: Adding a node type forces an edit to every visitor interface (and its implementations), so node set and operation set must evolve in step.
children() and the visitor's traversal must agree: a visitor that walks fields directly instead of children() drifts away from the generic passes.
The visitor's double dispatch cannot be inlined by the JIT as easily as a type switch, so heavy passes pay more dispatch overhead.
